title: Does anyone else develop games just for themselves?
author: gragert
selftext: I’ve been using ChatGPT and Claude to create a litany of games from side scrollers, tactics, RPGs, and Doom-style first-person shooters. I’m a doctoral student writing my dissertation on the iterative use of generative AI to develop literacy skills. Before that, I was just making the games for fun. I notice that many of the posts focus on trying to get others to play their games and/or sell them eventually, but I was wondering how many make games just for themselves. To me, the building is often more fun than playing the games. I like seeing what needs fixing, what could look better, and what mechanics it could use. I’ve probably started about a dozen games and “finished” (they’re never truly finished) about three. Has anyone else had this experience?

comments.author: SilliCarl
comments.body:
Yeah, my games are always made for me. That doesn't mean I'm AGAINST selling it, if it comes out good enough then I might.   
but thats not my goal. I've been making a game for 4 weeks and I've been having lots of fun playing and then iterating and developing it. I doubt it'll ever end up on the market, but I've played for 20 hours or so. Thats better than a lot of AAA games tbh.

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body:
That sounds like a great setup for your research, since the iteration loop is the part you're studying. A lot of people enjoy building more than playing, and AI tools make that loop much faster, so it's not surprising you end up with a dozen starts and three "finished" games.

If you ever want one person to play one, pick the one you're most proud of and show it to a friend. Watching someone else play is a different kind of fun from building, and it tends to show you the fix list you didn't know you had.

comments.author: flockbaygames
comments.body: Spotting what needs fixing is the actual skill I think, you have to play it and put into words why the jump feels floaty before the model can do anything with it, which sounds a lot like the literacy loop you're writing about. Would read that dissertation.

comments.author: psilocyan
comments.body:
Yeah, I'm making a game for my daughter, starring her. It's sort of a Zelda style top down adventure with combat, puzzles, and dialogue choices.

I love creating models and environments in Blender and I love seeing her face when she discovers some new secret I hid or laughs at an NPC's dialogue. It has no need to be on Steam lol.

I'll share it on this sub eventually, I'm only about a month in. 95% of my AI use has been helping with Unreal code, including some fluid / fur simulations. I take pride in meticulously modeling stuff and coming up with things like dungeon puzzles and quest ideas myself.

comments.author: Patient-Sprinkles920
comments.body: Yes, i have lot's a starts that kind of peter out. My first game I went pretty nuts with (maybe 1,000 hours). I launched on Play Store and nothing. I realized marketing is  horrible and probably not worth it. Since then I have started 4 games and finished 1. I play the one I finished all of the time, I have considered marketing it but the effort / reward equation seems pretty poor.

comments.author: Ok-Way-9449
comments.body:
I used chat GPT to create the character images based on a screen capture of grandchildren's head shots, then asked what weapon they wanted and colors and asked ChatGPT to create the image.  The grand kids love them. And i was listening to the 2 young ones fighting, and thought wouldn't it be nice if the could fight in a game.

Then I thought about Family Arena and wanted to see what ChatGPT and Claude could do and decided to give a small Prompt to ChatGPT and then the same prompt to Claude.  Below is what I gave them.

*I  want to create a game named Family Arena.  We will need an Arena similar the BattleHearts.  It will be for a PC.  The main difference it will be a two player game. One player enters from the left the other from the right,  They will walk in from off screen on right and left.   A timer will count down from 5 then the battle begins.  It will be  a 2 out 3 battles to be Victorious.*

*I will leave the development completely up to you I want to use the characters we created.  Come up with a plan I am open to anything at the start.*

It has been fun working with both.  One thing I regret doing is not archiving the beginning of the journey.    But I have the [gameplan.md](http://gameplan.md) files that both came up with and more documentation in the Doc folders of both. .ended up telling both I wanted a game to run on my home network and all the computers in the house to be able to play.   ChatGPT went with GoDot and Claude went with a Phaser 3 + Node.js/Socket.IO

Claude did a fantastic job with look feel and UI.   ChatGPT's is ok but no where as polished.  The base game is done. The Claude's version I have it recording fights between the grandchildren so I can have Claude balancing the game and may have to come up with a handicap so the 2nd and 3rd grade can compete with the older boys and been thinking about giving me a hidden god mode command so I don't lose all the time.

The most fun for me was finding rigs and working with ChatGPT to come up with a process for cutting the images up testing them and improving with each character.

All I can say it is a whole lot working with AI to create.

comments.author: MosskeepForest
comments.body:
Game developers do often enjoy their work. In the age of AI , being a game dev is a heck of a lot of fun. 

Being able to turn that into revenue and a living is an ideal scenario for people who enjoy it. 

Just imagine if you marketed the games you made and built a business and were earning 10k+ a month from it. That's why people are trying to get others to check out their work.... to let them grow and keep doing it and pay for more advanced tools and whatnot.
